theory.intro: In a triangle, **lowercase** letters name the sides and **uppercase** letters name the angles (and vertices). Each side is named with the same letter as the angle **opposite** it — so side $a$ is opposite angle $A$. An opposite side and angle never touch: the side does not reach that vertex.
facts: Side $a$ is opposite angle $A$, side $b$ is opposite angle $B$, and side $c$ is opposite angle $C$.
The side opposite an angle is the one that does **not** touch that angle's vertex.
The angle opposite a side is the one at the vertex the side does **not** reach — the corner across the triangle from it.
The naming letters are a free choice ($p$, $q$, $r$ or $x$, $y$, $z$ work too); what matters is that each lowercase side matches the uppercase angle across from it.
You can always name the opposite pair whatever way the triangle is turned — read the geometry, not the position on the page.

foundation.solution_text:
Angle $C$ sits at the bottom-left vertex. The side that does not touch that vertex is the one across from it, on the upper right.
The side opposite angle $C$ is $c$.

Side $e$ runs from $F$ to $D$, so it touches vertices $F$ and $D$ but not $E$.
The angle opposite side $e$ is $E$.

Angle $R$ is at the bottom-left vertex. The side across from it, not touching $R$, runs from $Q$ up to $P$.
The side opposite angle $R$ is $r$.

The $68^{\circ}$ angle is at the bottom-left vertex. It touches sides $g$ (the base) and $h$ (the left side).
The side that does not touch it, across the triangle, is $f$.

The $9$ cm side runs from $X$ to $Y$, touching vertices $X$ and $Y$. The vertex it does not reach is $Z$.
The angle opposite the $9$ cm side is $Z$.

Angle $L$ is at the bottom-left vertex, touched by sides $k$ (the base) and $m$ (the left side). The side across from it, from $K$ to $M$, is the one that does not touch $L$.
The side opposite angle $L$ is $l$.

development.solution_text:
The $112^{\circ}$ angle is at the left vertex, where sides $u$ and $t$ meet. The side across from it, joining the other two vertices, is $s$.
The side opposite the $112^{\circ}$ angle is $s$. (It is also the longest side, since the largest angle faces the longest side.)

development.question_text: A triangle is labelled $\triangle GHI$. Using the convention that each side is named with the lowercase letter of the angle opposite it, what is the name of the side opposite angle $H$?
development.solution_text:
The side opposite angle $H$ is the one that does not touch vertex $H$. By the naming convention it takes the lowercase form of that angle's letter.
The side opposite angle $H$ is $h$.

The $47^{\circ}$ angle is at the bottom-left vertex, touching sides $r$ (the base) and $t$ (the left side). The side across from it, on the right, is the one to relabel.
The side opposite the $47^{\circ}$ angle is $s$.

The $12$ m side runs from $S$ to $T$, touching vertices $S$ and $T$. The vertex it does not reach is $U$.
The angle opposite the $12$ m side is $U$.

The $40^{\circ}$ angle is at the bottom-left vertex, touched by sides $g$ and $f$. The side across from it, joining the top vertex to the bottom-right vertex, is $e$.
The side opposite the $40^{\circ}$ angle is $e$.

development.question_text: In $\triangle JKL$, which angle is opposite side $j$?
development.solution_text:
By the naming convention, the lowercase side $j$ is named after the angle across from it, which is written with the matching uppercase letter.
The angle opposite side $j$ is $J$.

practice.masteryOmitted: Identifying the opposite side or angle in a triangle is a single-step reading of the figure; the only harder work built on it — choosing and applying the sine, cosine or area rule — belongs to the dependent skills, so a mastery tier here would only restate the same recognition.
